result.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems
result.summary: Memory helps LLM-based multi-agent systems reuse experience, but stored advice can be flawed or applied in the wrong situation. Team-level success or failure alone cannot reliably show whether a memory needs correction or should not have been used. We propose DiscernMem, a training-free framework that improves both memory quality and memory use. To improve quality, Defect-Aware Memory Refinement (DMR) compares team executions with a single memory and with no memory, diagnoses rule defects, and tests repairs on current and earlier tasks to guard against losing previously useful behavior. To guide appropriate use, Boundary-Learning Meta-Memory (BLM) records each memory's past uses and effects, learning when its owner role should apply or avoid it based on task context and incoming messages. Together, these components help teams correct flawed experience while retaining useful rules that were applied incorrectly. Experiments with Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on four benchmarks show that DiscernMem achieves the highest average score on AutoGen, CAMEL, and MacNet, exceeding the strongest reported baselines by 0.51-4.32 points. It leads on code generation and symbolic planning across all three systems, including a PDDL score of 37.71 versus 28.48 on CAMEL.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练框架 DiscernMem：用 DMR 以「带单条记忆/无记忆」的执行对比诊断并修复记忆规则缺陷，并用 BLM 记录每条记忆的历史使用效果，学习在何种任务情境下应用或回避该记忆。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时使用记忆」的门控与对比式贡献归因，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据是否被调用、何时应停止调用的类比设计，但对象为纯文本多智能体记忆而非视觉 latent 状态，需较多核查。
